fig2_behavior_20260921: Performance across scale, reasoning and structured output. (a) Qwen2.5 scaling vs ToM2. (b) Archived seeker results, an audited historical Gemma standard hider cell, and audited Gemma thinking and OSS low-, medium- and high-effort hider cells (20 live matches of 50 rounds each). Gemma standard hider has 1,000 strict parses from an archived action-only run; its runtime differs from the new thinking run. Gemma thinking used 30 prespecified random fallbacks after truncated final-channel replies; OSS low/medium/high used 3/4/10 fallbacks after unparseable replies. All rounds remain in the deployed-system results. Intervals resample whole matches. (c) Separate seeker/hider comparisons, 20 live matches per condition, 50 rounds each. All four open-model hider arms and the Qwen3.6 seeker replacement are audited. Qwen3.6 seeker used brief structured output: 932 strict/68 action-only repairs, zero fallback; contrast +2.1, 95% CI [-1.0,5.4], inconclusive. Gemma hider includes 1/1000 random fallback (incomplete reply). Qwen3.6 hider: 1/1000 action-only repair, zero fallback. Historical hider prompt wording is role-ambiguous despite correct scoring instructions. Archived hider action-only baselines passed key/role/payoff/parse checks. GPT-5.4 uses fresh matched action-only/structured controls, identical candidate glossary, reasoning none/2048; not the medium-reasoning belief diagnostic. Prompt variants/budgets differ across families; Qwen3.6 uses brief output. Panel c uniformly omits error bars because verified match-level uncertainty is unavailable for all archived seeker conditions; audited intervals remain in the source table. (d) Qwen2.5-7B structured-output SFT against ToM2 and held-out ToM3. (e) Action-only and structured-output SFT transfer against GPT-5.4. Panels d-e use 20 matches/cell and archived intervals. ToM3 was absent from training and is a within-game higher-order transfer opponent. GPT in (e) is the opponent. Baselines and interventions are separate live runs, not common histories; historical comparisons retain runtime confounds. No universal structured-output benefit is established.
fig3_qwen_prediction_20260921: Fixed-history evaluation of Qwen2.5-7B. (a-b) Initial versus behavioral checkpoint300: 60 decision points from six matches. Action prediction uses 0/1 token confidence; belief reports estimate the opponent's prediction about us. Figure2 runtime tensor identity is not re-attested. (c) Both SFT conditions receive full history and opponent specification: ToM type, parameters (volatility=-2, b_temp=-1, bias=0), state-coordinate definitions and initial values. Neither receives the true current state or exact update equations. Outputs are action probability alone or state plus action probability. The latter receives true previous state during training and its own previous estimate during evaluation. Valid outputs:600/600 and582/600; invalid loss1. This is not a matched repair of (a). (d) Five-field supervision includes belief targets; not belief-only training. Initial marks each five-field run's own starting checkpoint, including the behavioral-SFT start. (e-f) Action-probability output throughout on the fresh R5 cohort. Extra training supplies specification on all examples or half (the remainder history only). Both start from (c)'s probability-output checkpoint. (e) Raw action-probability MSE by test information; (f) history-only MSE differences by opponent for the same continuations. Fresh60 matches,540 noninitial points/condition. History-only input removes type, parameters, state schema and initial values. (f) 95% match-bootstrap intervals, not training-seed uncertainty. Gains vary by opponent. These results do not establish mechanism understanding or live-transfer improvement.
fig4_gpt_diagnosis_20260921: GPT-5.4 medium: using opponent information differs from inferring it. q is opponent action probability; b is its belief about the focal player's action. (a) Exact rules supplied, 18 scheduled updates/level; missing outputs remain in the denominator. Own-state execution completes 5/6 chains. (b-c) Separate 24-match no-rule replication, 216 noninitial predictions/arm; S/H denote GPT seeker/hider. *The supervised control has independent task-specific training, not equal zero-shot prior information. (d-e) Matched interventions on six matches, 54 decisions/arm: panel d shows forecast MSE and panel e expected-regret differences. The same audit records 52/54 reference-best actions with true b versus 36/54 with self b; agreement is not plotted. Panel e: 95% paired match-bootstrap intervals; negative means reduced regret. (f) Six-match pilot: L1 reports q, L2 adds b, L3 adds a nested belief; memory retains own outputs. Depth is not opponent ToM level. Cells show MSE minus constant without MSE uncertainty intervals. Panels are distinct experiments, not a matched rules/no-rules ablation. Coverage is retry-assisted; fixed-history decisions are not live performance.
